sources_read: .qc-cache/coldwater-strict-2026-10-08-v16-full/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx :: 'Quality Checks' row #2 (A - instruction.md, instruction_preserves_natural_human_voice) and 'Internal Quality Checks' row #2 (same text, no extra annotation); Deterministic sheet note 'Voice and grammar are left to the rubric.'
evidence: Brief and all six notes keep one consistent first-person user voice with contractions and concrete personal context: instruction.md:1 "I'd like a small local playground... I often paste a long one-line experiment", instruction.md:5 "I start it with node /app/server.js... the way I'll use it"; behaviour.md:13 "My connection drops now and then"; security.md:3 "I run code I've pasted from all over the place"; ui.md:17 "I sometimes check things on my phone"; integration.md:5 "I won't run an install or build step". Grep of brief+notes for marketing gloss/LLM tells (seamless|robust|delve|leverage|ensure|comprehensive|intuitive|utiliz|furthermore|moreover|additionally|in order to|em dash|shall) returns no hits; only one 'must' (behaviour.md:13 'must not overwrite a newer save'). No bullet or numbered lists in any file (0 list lines per file); content is prose paragraphs, not a spec table. Sentence length varies from short ('Stop ends the current run straight away.' behaviour.md:7; 'Save code as plain text.' security.md:5) to long compound sentences, so cadence is not uniform. Voice does not shift between instruction.md and notes; integration.md:9 is the most impersonal ('Use SQLite for persistent records. The default database path is /app/app.db.') but that is runtime-contract wording and mirrors the template's integration.md, and it stays inside a first-person note. Template CHANGE_ME placeholders are fully replaced. Note (P3, not a defect): the notes repeatedly use a formulaic 'I do X, so please Y' justification device (overview.md:5, ui.md:7, ui.md:15, ui.md:17, behaviour.md:13 twice, security.md:3), several of which read as rationales manufactured for testable edge cases (network panel -> observable HTTP restores; dropped connection -> idempotent restore), and ui.md is a dense ~1000-word exhaustive edge-case catalogue with no terse fragments, which a strict client reader could perceive as polished/engineered rather than casual. This affects perceived authenticity only; it hides no requirement (each rationale also states the requirement plainly) and cannot change how a built app is graded, so there is no broken-app-passes or conforming-app-fails path through this row. Row is purely textual; no runtime evidence is required for it.
suggested_fix: Optional polish: vary or drop a few of the 'I X, so Y' rationales (e.g. behaviour.md:13 network-panel and dropped-connection lead-ins) and break one or two ui.md paragraphs into shorter, terser user asides; keep every stated requirement unchanged.
